strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#47776/PR#66321 in pandas: on buggy commit 95f2d5a36f15, np_can_hold_element accepts NA-free Int64/int64[pyarrow] values into uint64 targets (-1 wraps to 2**64-1) and Float64/double[pyarrow] 1e300 into float32 (becomes inf). Run the developer's two added tests; they should fail on buggy and pass on fixed revision.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era table entry in the evidence; they are unpinned and the strategy chooses current compatible releases
pyarrow is required only for the pyarrow-backend parametrizations and is unpinned, since no version is stated

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/dtypes/cast/test_can_hold_element.py::test_can_hold_element_ea_no_na_lossy_values and pandas/tests/indexing/test_indexing.py::TestiLocBaseIndependent::test_iloc_setitem_ea_dtype_lossy_raises (class name approximate; select with -k lossy)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 95f2d5a36f15: test_can_hold_element_ea_no_na_lossy_values fails at the assertion that can_hold_element(uint64 empty array, [-1,2,3] EA) is False, because it returns True; test_iloc_setitem_ea_dtype_lossy_raises fails because pytest.raises(TypeError) sees no exception from df.iloc[:,0]=lossy. On the fixed revision (with the PR applied, re-running np_can_hold_element on np.asarray(arr) after the _hasna check) both tests pass: lossy values are rejected and fitting values still assign inplace retaining dtype.
strategy.numerical_probe: can_hold_element(np.array([],dtype=np.uint64), pd.array([-1,2,3],dtype='Int64')) returns True on buggy and False on fixed; can_hold_element(np.array([],dtype=np.float32), pd.array([1e300,2.0],dtype='Float64')) returns True on buggy and False on fixed.

input_output_examples.input: signed EA holding -1 set into unsigned-integer numpy column
Float64 / double[pyarrow] value 1e300 set into narrower target float dtype
input_output_examples.expected_output: raise instead of silently overflowing to inf

risks: Behaviour is platform-independent integer/float arithmetic, but the test requires pyarrow for pyarrow parametrizations; without pyarrow those cases skip and the transition is only checked on numpy_nullable backend.

The PR's test asserts pytest.raises(TypeError, match='Invalid value') while the release note describes silent wrapping; the exception type on fixed revision must be confirmed by running the test, not assumed.
The buggy revision's exact behaviour (True from can_hold_element) is inferred from the test and bug description, not directly observed in the evidence.
Test class name in test_indexing.py is approximate; use -k lossy selection rather than a fixed class path.
No Python version is stated; choose a version supported by the pandas revision's build requirements.
Float overflow check relies on np.errstate(over='ignore') semantics; warnings-as-errors configuration could alter the outcome, so do not promote warnings to errors when running.
Mathematical losslessness is only implied by examples, so the fix's exact range rule is not independently verified by this plan.

oracle.reference_source: developer test assertions in the PR diff
oracle.why: Transition is decided by boolean can_hold_element results and exception presence, not numeric tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: can_hold_element returns True for -1 into uint64 and 1e300 into float32, so the 'assert not' fails; the iloc setitem performs silent wrap/overflow so pytest.raises(TypeError) reports no exception raised.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: Fixed np_can_hold_element rejects out-of-range NA-free EA values, so can_hold_element returns False and the iloc assignment raises TypeError 'Invalid value'; fitting values assign inplace and the frame matches the expected dtype.
